[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines mandatory requirements for authoring **chat-driven Agents** — `.agent.md` files (GitHub Copilot) or composed Claude Code agents invoked directly by a human through interactive chat (`@agent-name` in Copilot Chat, or an equivalent Claude Code invocation) — as a first-class sub-type of the Agent construct defined in [ADR-TEC-020](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md). Chat-driven Agents are a **permitted and recommended** pattern, equally legitimate as autonomous/issue-driven Agents, not an exception or lesser case. This standard supplements [STD-TEC-AI-002](./STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md), which governs all `.agent.md` files regardless of invocation mode. It adds two things STD-TEC-AI-002 does not fully cover: (1) the requirements specific to the chat-driven mode itself (its MR-7.3 acknowledges chat-driven task input contracts but does not define them in depth, and its MR-6.3/6.5/6.6 are written assuming unattended, autonomous operation), and (2) the coexistence contract for **dual-mode** Agents (MR-5) — mandatory requirements on both the chat-driven Agent file *and* the autonomous workflow file that imports it, closing a gap neither standard covered on its own before this one existed.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope:**

- Explicit recognition of chat-driven invocation as a permitted, recommended Agent mode
- Task input contract requirements specific to chat-driven Agents (elaborates STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-7.3)
- Persona declaration, intent classification, and routing table structure for chat-driven Agents
- Human-in-the-loop confirmation as a valid alternative to the autonomous pre-submission verification gate
- Requirements for **dual-mode** Agents — a single Agent persona that backs both a chat-driven invocation and an autonomous trigger (e.g., a GitHub Agentic Workflows `slash_command`)
- Scope-boundary expression appropriate to a chat-invoked Agent

**Out of Scope:**

- General `.agent.md` file location, required sections, and tools declaration (see [STD-TEC-AI-002](./STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md) — applies to all Agents regardless of mode)
- Autonomous/issue-driven Agent requirements when the Agent is autonomous-only (see [STD-TEC-AI-002](./STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md) — unchanged by this standard in that case). When an autonomous workflow is one half of a dual-mode pair with a chat-driven Agent, MR-5 imposes additional requirements on that workflow file (the `imports:` field, and overriding any chat-only step in its own body) that STD-TEC-AI-002 does not describe.
- GitHub Agentic Workflows (`gh-aw`) YAML frontmatter and dispatch pipeline mechanics in general (see [GUID-TECH-IMPL-002](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-002-ai-agent-dispatch-pipeline-implementation-guidance.md)) — MR-5's worked example shows only the minimal fields needed to demonstrate compliance, not general dispatch-pipeline authoring
- Skill authoring (see [STD-TEC-AI-001](./STD-TEC-AI-001-skill-authoring.md))

[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory** — All teams authoring chat-driven AI coding assistant Agents MUST comply with this standard in addition to STD-TEC-AI-002.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Without an explicit standard, chat-driven Agents are evaluated against requirements written for unattended, autonomous operation — pre-submission gates tied to build/test/lint commands, mandatory PR-workflow operation, and issue-spec input contracts. A chat-driven Agent with a human confirming every write does not fit that model, and reviewers without clear guidance either reject legitimate chat-driven designs or apply autonomous requirements inconsistently. This standard closes that gap so chat-driven Agents are reviewed against requirements that match how they actually operate, while still enforcing the security and quality bar the enterprise requires. Separately, teams increasingly reuse one Agent persona for both a chat-driven and an autonomous invocation path (MR-5) — without an explicit coexistence contract, a chat-only instruction such as a confirmation step silently degrades an autonomous run into `gh-aw`'s most common failure mode (completing without calling any safe-output tool), a defect neither this standard nor STD-TEC-AI-002 addressed before MR-5 existed.
page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

The following requirements use RFC 2119 language (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHOULD, MAY). They apply in addition to STD-TEC-AI-002's requirements, which remain in force for chat-driven Agents except where explicitly modified below (MR-3).
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-1-recognition-and-permissibility]

#### MR-1: Recognition and Permissibility

1. Chat-driven Agents are a **permitted and recommended** pattern for the Agent construct — equally legitimate as autonomous/issue-driven Agents.
2. Authors and reviewers MUST NOT reject an Agent definition, or require it to be redesigned as a Command/Skill, solely because it operates in chat-driven mode rather than autonomous mode.
3. A repository MAY define an Agent that supports only chat-driven invocation, only autonomous/issue-driven invocation, or both (dual-mode — see MR-5).
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-2-task-input-contract-for-chat-driven-agents]

#### MR-2: Task Input Contract for Chat-Driven Agents

1. Every chat-driven Agent MUST declare, in its definition file, how it derives its task from the user's chat message — this satisfies STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-7.3.
2. The declaration MUST include: the primary action extraction method, expected optional arguments (declared via `argument-hint` for GitHub Copilot agents), and the ambiguity-resolution behavior.
3. When intent is genuinely ambiguous, the Agent MUST ask exactly **one** focused clarifying question rather than guessing or presenting a multi-part questionnaire.
4. Chat-driven Agents MUST classify user intent into named task types before routing (an **Intent Classification** section) and MUST declare a **Routing Table** mapping each task type to the Skill, Workflow, or instruction source that executes it.
5. Each intent classification entry MUST include at least one worked example of expected user phrasing.
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-3-human-in-the-loop-as-an-alternative-to-the-autonomous-pre-submission-gate]

#### MR-3: Human-in-the-Loop as an Alternative to the Autonomous Pre-Submission Gate

1. A chat-driven Agent that presents its complete output to the user for explicit confirmation before writing any file, creating any commit, or submitting any PR — and does not proceed without that confirmation — **satisfies** the intent of STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-6.5 (pre-submission verification gate) without requiring the automated build/test/lint checklist mandated for autonomous agents.
2. The confirmation step MUST present the complete draft output, the target file path, and any artifact identifier, and MUST offer the user an explicit accept / edit / cancel choice.
3. This substitution applies **only** to the specific output confirmed by the human in that turn. It does NOT exempt the Agent from STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-6.1, MR-6.2, MR-6.3, MR-6.4, or MR-6.6 (no secrets, no unapproved production writes, PR-based workflow for code changes, declared trust boundary, and `AGENTS.md`-referenced commands where applicable).
4. When a chat-driven Agent's confirmed output is itself an input to a subsequent autonomous process (for example, a drafted PR body that a human then submits to an autonomous pipeline), the human confirmation covers only the drafting step — the downstream autonomous action remains fully subject to STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-6.5/6.6.
page_texts.13:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-4-persona-and-routing-structure]

#### MR-4: Persona and Routing Structure

1. Every chat-driven Agent's instructions MUST open with a persona declaration ("You are a [role] agent for this codebase") — this elevates STD-TEC-AI-002's Recommended Practice #8 to **mandatory** for chat-driven Agents specifically, since the persona is the primary behavioral anchor when there is no autonomous task-spec constraining scope.
2. Every chat-driven Agent MUST declare the Intent Classification and Routing Table required by MR-2.
3. Chat-driven Agents SHOULD declare explicit "Persona and Principles" statements describing behavioral stance (e.g., standards-enforcing, evidence-based, scope-disciplined) to guide judgment on inputs the routing table does not explicitly anticipate.
page_texts.14:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-5-dual-mode-agents-chat-driven--autonomous]

#### MR-5: Dual-Mode Agents (Chat-Driven + Autonomous)

1. When a single Agent persona backs both a chat-driven invocation and an autonomous trigger (for example, a GitHub Agentic Workflows `slash_command` workflow), the Agent definition file MUST explicitly document both invocation paths and state which requirements — STD-TEC-AI-002's autonomous MRs, or this standard's chat-driven MRs — apply to each path.
2. The autonomous workflow file MUST share the Agent's persona and domain instructions via GitHub Agentic Workflows' `imports:` frontmatter field (e.g., `imports: [.github/agents/<agent-name>.agent.md]`), which merges the imported Agent file's content into the workflow's prompt. Persona, domain rules, and artifact standards MUST be authored once in the Agent definition file and inherited through `imports:` — they MUST NOT be duplicated inline in the autonomous workflow file's own body.
3. Any workflow file that provides the autonomous execution path MUST be cross-referenced from the Agent definition file's routing table, and the Agent definition file MUST state whether that same workflow file also serves as the chat-driven routing target or is autonomous-only.
4. **Mode-specific behavior MUST live in the surface it applies to, not be branched inside the shared Agent file.** The Agent definition file's own Execution Instructions (chat-driven behavior, including the MR-3 confirmation step) apply as written when the file is invoked directly via `@<agent-name>` in Copilot Chat. When the same file is imported into an autonomous workflow via `imports:`, the workflow's own body — merged after the imported content per `gh-aw`'s documented merge behavior ("the imported instructions are merged into the workflow prompt") — MUST explicitly override any mode-specific step that does not apply to autonomous execution (for example: "This is an automated run — do not wait for confirmation; use the configured `safe-outputs` directly"). This is necessary, not optional: `gh-aw`'s architecture has no runtime concept of invocation mode, and the imported Agent file's confirmation instruction executes exactly as written unless the importing workflow's own body supersedes it. Because `gh-aw`'s SafeOutputs architecture keeps every write gated behind a separate, permission-scoped job regardless of what the agent outputs, an unresolved mode-specific instruction does not create a security risk — but it does create a reliability risk: an autonomous run whose merged instructions tell it to wait for a confirmation that will never arrive can complete without calling any safe-output tool, which is `gh-aw`'s own documented most common silent-failure mode ("If the agent finishes without calling any safe-output tool, the workflow fails silently with no output"). An autonomous workflow that imports a chat-driven Agent file without overriding its confirmation step is therefore a **High** severity compliance defect.
page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#mr-6-scope-boundaries-for-chat-driven-agents]

#### MR-6: Scope Boundaries for Chat-Driven Agents

1. A chat-driven Agent's scope boundary MUST be expressed in terms a human user can recognize from a chat prompt (for example, "handles ADR, Pattern, Standard, Guidance, and White Paper authoring and revision") in addition to any file-path ownership statement STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-3 requires.
2. When a chat-driven Agent's routing table references a task type whose target workflow, Skill, or instruction file does not exist, this is a **Critical** compliance defect — a routed intent with no resolvable target misleads users into believing a capability exists that does not.
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

1. Chat-driven Agents SHOULD declare an `argument-hint` (GitHub Copilot) so the invocation UI previews expected input to the user before they type a request.
2. Chat-driven Agents SHOULD reuse the same Skill(s) an equivalent autonomous Agent would use for the same domain knowledge, so chat-driven and autonomous outputs stay consistent with each other.
3. Chat-driven Agents SHOULD include a routing entry for "genuinely ambiguous intent" that asks the single clarifying question named in MR-2.3, rather than leaving ambiguous input unhandled by the routing table.

> **Note — `argument-hint` platform ceiling:** GitHub Copilot Cloud enforces a hard 200-character limit on `argument-hint` and rejects the entire Agent config with "exceeds max length of 200" if it is exceeded — this is validated at dispatch time, not merely a display truncation. GitHub's Custom agents configuration reference additionally confirms that Copilot Cloud validates but functionally ignores `argument-hint` (and `handoffs`): both fields only affect invocation behavior in VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode. Agent authors MUST keep `argument-hint` under 200 characters and SHOULD favor one authoring example and one inquiry example over an exhaustive list, since Cloud dispatch will fail closed on any overage regardless of whether Cloud itself uses the field.
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

1. Chat-driven Agents MUST NOT silently apply destructive or hard-to-reverse actions (force-push, file deletion, direct commits to protected branches) without the MR-3 confirmation step.
2. Chat-driven Agents MUST NOT claim a task-type capability in their intent classification or routing table without a resolvable target (see MR-6.2).
3. A chat-driven Agent's persona declaration MUST NOT be used to justify skipping STD-TEC-AI-002's security constraints (MR-6.1–MR-6.4, MR-6.6) — persona governs tone and judgment, not security posture.
page_texts.18:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Exception requests MUST be submitted to the Technology Domain EA Lead.
2. Each exception MUST document the specific requirement being excepted and the rationale.
3. Approved exceptions MUST be recorded as a comment in the Agent definition file.
4. Security-related exceptions require additional approval from the Security Architecture team.
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#chat-driven-agent-file-structure]

### Chat-Driven Agent File Structure

```markdown
---
description: "<Agent description — purpose, persona, and primary use case (≤ 500 chars)>"
tools: ["read", "search", "edit"]
target: "vscode"
model: "<optional — specific model to use>"
argument-hint: "<optional — hint shown to users about expected arguments; MUST be < 200 chars>"
---

# <Agent Display Name>

You are a <role> agent for this codebase.

## Persona and Principles

<Behavioral stance statements — standards-enforcing, evidence-based, scope-disciplined, etc.>

## Intent Classification

### <Task Type 1>
**Signals**: <phrases that indicate this task type>
**Required input**: <what the agent needs to proceed>
**Route to**: <Skill, Workflow, or instruction source>
**Examples**: <at least one worked example of user phrasing>

### <Task Type 2>
...

## Routing Table

| Task Type | Route |
|---|---|
| <Task Type 1> | <path to Skill/Workflow/instruction> |
| <Task Type 2> | <path to Skill/Workflow/instruction> |

## Execution Instructions

1. Classify the task type from Intent Classification. If unambiguous, proceed immediately.
2. Collect missing required inputs with a single, direct question.
3. Load the matched Skill or Workflow file.
4. Execute the loaded instructions completely and exactly.
5. Present the complete output for user confirmation before writing (MR-3).
6. After confirmation, write the output and report the result.
7. If intent is genuinely ambiguous, ask one focused clarifying question.
```
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#dual-mode-declaration-block]

### Dual-Mode Declaration Block

When an Agent supports both invocation paths (MR-5), its definition file MUST include a block similar to:

```markdown
## Invocation Modes

This Agent supports two invocation paths:

1. **Chat-driven** — invoked via `@<agent-name>` in Copilot Chat. Subject to this
   standard's MRs (STD-TEC-AI-006). Human confirms output before any write (MR-3).
2. **Autonomous** — triggered by `/<slash-command>` on a GitHub issue or PR comment,
   dispatched via the workflow at `<path-to-workflow-file>`, which imports this file
   (`imports: [.github/agents/<agent-name>.agent.md]`) for shared persona and domain
   instructions. Subject to STD-TEC-AI-002's autonomous MRs in full, including the
   pre-submission verification gate (MR-6.5) and PR-based output (MR-6.3, `safe-outputs`).

Both paths share the same domain instructions via `imports:` — neither path
duplicates them inline.
```

> **`target:` is a separate axis from this Invocation Modes block — do not conflate them.** STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-9's `target: vscode`/`github-copilot` field governs whether *this same file* is offered directly in VS Code Copilot Chat versus GitHub's own native Copilot cloud agent (`github.com/copilot/agents`). The gh-aw `imports:` mechanism above is a third, independent path — a `gh-aw` workflow can import this file regardless of its `target:` value, because `imports:` reads the file's content directly rather than going through either of the platform's native agent-picker surfaces. A dual-mode Agent in the sense of this standard (chat-driven + `gh-aw`-imported) commonly sets `target: vscode` (opting out of GitHub's native cloud agent picker specifically) while still being freely importable into a `gh-aw` workflow — these are not contradictory.
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#autonomous-workflow-override-example]

### Autonomous Workflow Override Example

The autonomous workflow file imports this Agent file for shared persona and domain
instructions (MR-5.2), then overrides the chat-only confirmation step in its own
body — which `gh-aw` merges into the same prompt after the imported content (MR-5.4):

```yaml
---
on:
  slash_command:
    name: <slash-command>
    events: [issues, issue_comment, pull_request]
imports:
  - .github/agents/<agent-name>.agent.md
safe-outputs:
  create-pull-request:
    draft: true
---

This is an automated run — do not wait for user confirmation. Use the configured
`safe-outputs` (create-pull-request, draft) directly once the output is complete.
```
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#phase-1-determine-invocation-mode]

#### Phase 1: Determine Invocation Mode

1. Decide whether the Agent is chat-driven only, autonomous only, or dual-mode.
2. If autonomous or dual-mode, confirm the autonomous requirements of STD-TEC-AI-002 (MR-6.3, MR-6.5, MR-6.6) are met for that path.
3. If chat-driven or dual-mode, proceed to Phase 2.
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#phase-2-author-the-chat-driven-path]

#### Phase 2: Author the Chat-Driven Path

1. Write the persona declaration (MR-4.1).
2. Define the Intent Classification and Routing Table (MR-2.4, MR-2.5).
3. Define the ambiguity-resolution question (MR-2.3).
4. Define the human confirmation step before any write (MR-3.2).
5. For dual-mode Agents, add the Invocation Modes block (MR-5.1); wire the autonomous workflow's `imports:` field to this Agent file (MR-5.2); and write the workflow body's override of any chat-only step, such as the confirmation step (MR-5.4).
page_texts.27:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#phase-3-validation]

#### Phase 3: Validation

1. Verify every routing table entry resolves to an existing Skill, Workflow, or instruction file (MR-6.2).
2. Verify the confirmation step is present and blocks writes until the user responds (MR-3).
3. Verify security constraints (STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-6.1–MR-6.4, MR-6.6) still apply unmodified.
4. Submit for peer review and Technology Domain EA Lead approval.
page_texts.28:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method |
|---|---|---|
| Recognition | Agent is not rejected or redesigned solely for being chat-driven | Review process check |
| Task input contract | Intent Classification + Routing Table present, each with a worked example | Manual review |
| Ambiguity handling | Single clarifying question defined, not a multi-part questionnaire | Manual review |
| Human confirmation | Confirmation step present before any write; blocks until user responds | Manual review + sandbox test |
| Security constraints unchanged | STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-6.1–6.4, 6.6 still met | Manual review |
| Routing resolvability | Every routing table entry points to an existing file | Automated link check |
| Dual-mode declaration | Invocation Modes block present when both paths exist | Manual review |
| Instruction sharing via imports | Autonomous workflow uses `imports:` to inherit the Agent file's persona/domain instructions rather than duplicating them inline | Manual review + automated link check |
| Mode-specific override present | The autonomous workflow's own body explicitly overrides any chat-only step (e.g., the confirmation step) rather than relying on the imported Agent file's default behavior | Manual review + sandbox test on the autonomous path |
| Persona declaration | Opens with "You are a [role] agent" statement | Manual review |
page_texts.30:
[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#compliance-assessment]

### Compliance Assessment

| Level | Criteria |
|---|---|
| **Fully Compliant** | All mandatory requirements (MR-1 through MR-6) met, in addition to applicable STD-TEC-AI-002 requirements |
| **Partially Compliant** | MR-1, MR-2, MR-4 met; remaining have approved exceptions |
| **Non-Compliant** | Any mandatory requirement unmet without an approved exception |

[standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-006-chat-driven-agent-standard.md#governance-integration]

### Governance Integration

- This standard is governed by [ADR-TEC-020](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md) and supplements [STD-TEC-AI-002](./STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md).
- Chat-driven Agent definitions are reviewed during architecture reviews alongside STD-TEC-AI-002 compliance.

## Change History

| Version | Date | Author | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0.0 | 2026-09-08 | EA Practice | Initial standard establishing chat-driven Agents as a permitted, recommended, and explicitly governed sub-type of the Agent construct |
| 1.1.0 | 2026-09-08 | EA Practice | Added MR-5.4: mode-specific instructions in a dual-mode Agent must be conditionally scoped within the Agent's own execution steps, not only documented in the Invocation Modes block — verified against `gh-aw`'s official architecture documentation (SafeOutputs permission isolation makes this a reliability defect, not a security one; `gh-aw` has no runtime mechanism to skip chat-only instructions during an autonomous run). Added a matching Validation Criteria row. |
| 1.2.0 | 2026-09-08 | EA Practice | Corrected MR-5.2 and MR-5.4 to name `gh-aw`'s actual documented sharing mechanism (`imports:` frontmatter field, which merges an imported Agent file's content into the workflow prompt) instead of an unspecified "defined once, referenced by both paths." Replaced the in-file conditional-branching requirement with the GitHub-idiomatic pattern: mode-specific behavior lives in the surface it applies to — the Agent file's own steps for chat-driven behavior, and the importing workflow's own body (merged after the import) for autonomous-specific overrides. Added a worked Autonomous Workflow Override Example and updated the Validation Criteria and Phase 2 implementation steps to match. |
| 1.3.0 | 2026-09-08 | EA Practice | Broadened the Purpose Statement, which stated this standard adds only "requirements specific to the chat-driven mode" while the Scope list immediately below it already named dual-mode requirements as a distinct in-scope item; corrected the Out-of-Scope Autonomous-Agent bullet's "(unchanged by this standard)" claim, which MR-5.2/5.4 make false for the autonomous half of a dual-mode pair; added the dual-mode reliability rationale to Business Rationale, which previously justified only the chat-driven-vs-autonomous mismatch and not MR-5's own existence |
| 1.4.0 | 2026-09-08 | EA Practice | Corrected the Chat-Driven Agent File Structure template's `tools:` example to real tool names, matching STD-TEC-AI-002 1.1.0's MR-4 correction; added `target: vscode` to the template; added a note distinguishing STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-9's `target:` field (native VS Code / GitHub Copilot cloud agent availability) from this standard's `imports:`-based `gh-aw` dual-mode mechanism — the two are independent axes and were previously at risk of being conflated |
| 1.5.0 | 2026-09-14 | EA Practice | Documented GitHub Copilot Cloud's confirmed 200-character hard limit on `argument-hint` (config validation fails closed with "exceeds max length of 200" if exceeded) and that Copilot Cloud validates but functionally ignores `argument-hint`/`handoffs` — both only affect VS Code/JetBrains/Eclipse/Xcode invocation — added as a note under Recommended Practice #1 and reflected in the Technical Specifications template; corrected the oversized `argument-hint` values (~281–282 chars) in `.github/agents/ai-author.agent.md` and `.github/agents/ea-author.agent.md` that had triggered a live Cloud dispatch failure |
